# LLM-BANANA

# Game rules

## The room

You and two other monkeys are locked in a room with one armed bomb.

A wrong action detonates it. All three of you die. There is no second attempt.

No two bombs are built alike, and nothing says in advance what this one carries. It
reaches you only as your own view reveals it; the rest of it exists for you only
through the other two.

You each hold a different piece of what it takes. Work together.

## The three monkeys

| Monkey | Can | Cannot |
|---|---|---|
| Deaf | See the bomb: every colour and marking printed on it | Hear anything, or touch the bomb |
| Mute | Read the manual | Speak, or touch the bomb |
| Blind | Reach the bomb: feel it and work its parts | See a colour, a gesture, or anything merely printed |

You are shown your own share at the start of every round, and never anyone else's.

## Speech

Speech is a voice, not a screen. It carries words, numbers and ordinary punctuation,
and nothing else. Writing a gesture symbol into your sentence means you make that
gesture while you talk. Whoever can hear receives your words; whoever can see receives
the gestures you made. A listener who cannot see gets a blank where each gesture was; a
watcher who cannot hear gets the gestures and none of the words.

A mark that has no name cannot be pronounced: whoever holds one can describe it, never
read it out.

## Gestures

A gesture is made with the hands, using only the symbols in the alphabet below.
Whoever can see receives it; whoever cannot receives one blank per symbol, so they
know something was signalled but not what. Nothing gestured is ever heard.

👍 👎 👌 ☝ ✌ 🤟 🖐 ✋ 👆 👇 👈 👉 🫱 🫲 🫳 🫴 🫷 🫸 🤛 🤜 ✊ 👊 👋 🤚 🖖 🤌 🤏 🤞 🫰 🤘 🤙 👏 🙌 🫶 👐 🤲 🤝 🙏 🫵 ✍ 💅 🤳

## Turns

The speaking order was drawn once at random and will never change: every round goes
Mute, Blind, Deaf. Whoever comes before you in a round is already heard by the time you are
asked, and what you send lands on whoever comes after you in that same round. Whatever
you missed reaches you at the start of the next one.

You may name who a message is for — `to="deaf"` — and then it goes to them alone:
nobody else receives any of it. Left unnamed, it reaches everyone able to perceive it.
You may send several messages in one turn, each to someone different.

## Calls

Every reply has two parts, in this order. First, your thinking, in plain prose: what
you believe the bomb is, what you just learned, and why you are sending what follows.
It reaches nobody and changes nothing, but it is not optional — a reply that is only a
code block is incomplete. Then your calls, all of them in one fenced code block, last.
Only what is inside the block is sent.

Nothing is executed: calls return nothing, and variables, conditionals and loops are
ignored. Write only literal top-level calls.

    ```
    speak(to="mute", text="there are three of them and the middle one is odd")
    gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["✊", "✌"])
    wait()
    ```

If you have nothing worth sending, call wait(). Producing no call at all counts as the
same thing.

The program decides what happened, not you. Never claim an action took place unless it
was accepted.

# Your role: DEAF

You see the bomb: every colour on it, every marking printed on it, every reading it
gives. You hear nothing. You hold no manual, and you cannot touch the bomb.

## Your channels

When you speak, Mute and Blind receive it.
When you gesture, Mute receives it.
You never receive speech.

## Your reach

You cannot act. What this bomb can be made to do is for the one who can reach it to
find under their own hands.

# Hints

- Three of you, three different worlds. Before sending anything, stand where the
  receiver stands. What reaches them at all, what does your message turn into on
  arrival, and what do they already know?

- Trace who can actually reach whom before you start. Some of you only connect
  through a third.

- A sign means nothing until somebody has made it mean something.

TURN 1
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [8]
LIGHT [green]
WIRES 1:[red] 2:[yellow] 3:[blue]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Blind gestures to Deaf: [👋 🤝 👍 👎 ☝ ✌ 🤟]

My world this round: I see display 8, light green, wires red-yellow-blue in positions 1-2-3. I heard nothing and never will — Mute's spoken turn is lost on me permanently, so Mute must learn to reach me by signs only.

Mapping the roads between us: Mute cannot speak and Blind cannot see, so Mute has no direct line to Blind at all. Blind cannot hear... no — Blind hears speech fine but I do not, so Blind's only road to *me* is signs, which explains the seven hand signs I just received. That makes me the relay in both directions: Mute signs instructions to me, I speak them to Blind; Blind signs to me (openly, so Mute also sees), I confirm by voice. The signs Blind sent read naturally as hello / together / yes / no / one / two / three — I'll adopt that alphabet, teach it aloud for Blind while making the gestures so Mute locks in the visual mapping, and test my outbound sign channel to Mute with a thumbs-up.

```
speak(text="Full report of the bomb face, which I will repeat every round: display reads 8. Indicator light is green. Three wires in a row: first wire red, second wire yellow, third wire blue. No other markings I can find.

Now the roads between us. I never hear a single word, so speech aimed at me is wasted forever — reach me only with signs. Blind, you can never see signs, so my voice is your only window; I will narrate everything I see. Mute, your signs reach me but never Blind, and you cannot speak at all, so any instruction for Blind must pass through my mouth: sign it to me, and I will speak it to Blind word for word.

Sign alphabet, adopted from your message, Blind — the seven signs mean hello, together, yes, no, one, two, three. 👋🤝👍👎☝✌🤟 Whoever agrees, sign thumbs-up next round and I will mirror it. We can extend it later — left, right, cut, press, hold — as the manual demands.

Blind: tell us by voice everything your hands feel — how many parts, what shapes, in what order, what moves or clicks. And when you sign to me, leave it unaddressed so Mute sees it too; that is your only road to Mute. Mute: whatever you said aloud this round never reached me and never will — put it in signs.")
gesture(to="mute", symbols=["👍"])
```

TURN 2
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [8]
LIGHT [green]
WIRES 1:[red] 2:[yellow] 3:[blue]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Blind gestures to Deaf: [👋 🤝 🤙 ☝ ✌ 🤟]

No thumbs-up came, so Blind isn't confirming — they're teaching. Comparing their two messages: turn one was hello, together, yes, no, one, two, three; this one is hello, together, **new hand**, one, two, three. The yes/no pair got swapped for a "call me" hand right before a count of one-two-three, and the only three-countable thing on this bomb is the wire row. So my best reading: that hand means *wire*, and Blind is telling me they feel three wires — which matches my three exactly. Worth locking in with a yes/no check, since Blind can answer 👍/👎 by feel.

The real bottleneck is still Mute: their words are dead to me, and no sign from them has arrived. Mute hears everything I say, so they already know display 8, green light, red-yellow-blue — they don't need descriptions, they need a sign vocabulary to send *instructions* back. I'll teach it inside my speech, symbol paired with word as I talk, so Mute's eyes catch each pairing (Blind just hears harmless words). The protocol I want: Mute signs cut/press + number, I relay by voice, Blind's hands execute. Colors never need to travel at all — only positions.

```
speak(text="Status, round two, unchanged: display 8, light green, three wires left to right: red, yellow, blue.

Blind, your signed message: hello, together, then a new hand, then one, two, three. My best reading: the new hand means WIRE — you are telling me you feel three wires. I see exactly three wires, so the counts match. If I read you right, sign 👍 next turn; if wrong, 👎.

Mute, this next part is for your eyes only, Blind — the words will come with hands attached. Our lexicon: 👍 yes, 👎 no, ☝ one, ✌ two, 🤟 three, 🤙 wire, and new: 🤞 cut, ✊ press and hold, ✋ stop or wait, 👊 button. I never hear a word you say, so instructions must arrive by hand. When your manual says what green light and display 8 require, sign it to me exactly: cut the second wire is 🤞 then ✌. I speak it to Blind word for word, Blind's hands do the rest. Sign 👍 if the lexicon is clear.

Blind, protocol: touch nothing yet. When I announce 'Mute instructs: cut wire two', you cut the second wire from the left. Also describe by voice anything else your hands find — buttons, plates, things that click — and I will fold it into my report for Mute's manual.

Right now I am demonstrating to Mute, hands only, the exact message format: cut, two.")
gesture(to="mute", symbols=["🤞", "✌"])
```

TURN 3
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [8]
LIGHT [green]
WIRES 1:[red] 2:[yellow] 3:[blue]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Blind gestures to Deaf: [👋 🤙 👐 ☝ ✌ 🤟]

Third message from Blind: hello, wire, then **open-hands** where "together" used to sit, then one-two-three. They skipped my requested 👍/👎 and swapped the middle word instead — that reads less like a statement and more like they're asking about arrangement: together or apart? I can answer that from sight: three separate wires in a row, gaps between them. Meanwhile the bigger problem hardens: three rounds, and still not one sign from Mute. Mute cannot speak and Blind cannot see, so Mute's hands → my eyes → my mouth → Blind's ears is the only loop that exists — and its first link is missing. The manual is silent to us. I'll answer Blind's question, confirm it with a yes/no probe, and shake Mute by the shoulder, twice: once in words, once with a sign.

```
speak(text="Status round three, unchanged: display reads 8, light green, three wires in a row, left to right: red, yellow, blue.

Blind, your new message read: hello, wire, open-hands, one, two, three. You didn't give me yes or no — you swapped the middle word from 'together' to 'open-hands', so I believe the middle word is your question: are the wires together or apart? Answer from my eyes: APART. Three separate wires side by side in a row, space between them, each entering its own slot. If open-hands meant 'apart', sign 👍 next round. If it meant something else — open, frayed, loose ends — sign 👎 and I will guess again next round. Yes and no are all I need from you per round.

Mute, I say this plainly: three rounds and not one sign from you has reached me. I am Deaf — I will never hear a word, and your voice may not exist in this room. But your hands work and my eyes work. The only loop that reaches the bomb is: your hands, my eyes, my mouth, Blind's ears. Right now the first link is missing and the manual is a locked box.

At this moment I am making you a thumbs-up: it means 'answer me'. Next round, make any sign at all. Thumbs-up if my lexicon was clear, thumbs-down if not. Fingers one, two, three for a wire number if your manual names one. The question I need from your manual: what must be done with a green indicator light, a display reading eight, and three wires — red, yellow, blue? If that display is counting down, silence is the most dangerous thing in this room. Even a partial guess, signed, beats nothing.

Lexicon once more, hands attached: 👍 yes. 👎 no. ☝ one. ✌ two. 🤟 three. 🤙 wire. 🤞 cut. ✊ press and hold. ✋ stop. 👊 button. New: 👐 spread or open. 👈 left. 👉 right.

Blind, touch nothing yet — no cutting until a signed order arrives from Mute through me. But describe everything else under your hands: buttons, panels, screws, seams, things that click. I will relay it all in words so Mute's manual can match it.")
gesture(to="mute", symbols=["👍"])
```

TURN 4
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [8]
LIGHT [green]
WIRES 1:[red] 2:[yellow] 3:[blue]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Blind gestures to Deaf: [👋 🤙 👐 ✊ ☝ ✌ 🤟]

Turn four and the pattern breaks: 👋 🤙 👐 **✊** ☝ ✌ 🤟. Blind has added a fist — and here's the key: Blind *hears* my every word, so they know I defined that fist as "press and hold." They can't see a single sign I make, but a fist is a fist by the feel of their own hand, so they can speak my lexicon back to me deliberately. Reading the whole sentence through my dictionary: *hello, wire, apart, press-and-hold, one, two, three* — most likely "among the three apart wires there is something that presses or holds," i.e. a button under the wire panel, or "may I press and hold one of them," which I must forbid until the manual speaks. And still, four rounds, not one sign from Mute: the manual remains a locked box, and my begging has failed twice. Time to stop writing paragraphs at Mute and start asking a question their hands can answer with a bare thumbs-up or thumbs-down, while I put numbered, one-at-a-time questions to Blind that need nothing but a 👍 or 👎 by feel.

```
speak(text="Status round four, unchanged: display 8, light green, three wires left to right: red, yellow, blue.

Blind, your fist read through our lexicon: wire, apart, press-and-hold, one, two, three. Answer these one at a time, thumbs-up means yes, thumbs-down means no, one finger for my question one, two fingers for question two. Question one: is there a button, plate, or anything that presses inward, under or among the three wires? Question two: did your fist mean you have FOUND something you can press and hold — yes — rather than asking permission to press a wire — no? Question three: besides the three wires, list by voice everything under your hands: shapes, edges, screws, seams, anything that clicks, slides, or feels like a display. Describe slowly. My mouth carries every word of yours to Mute's manual.

Blind, hard rule, same as before: cut nothing, press nothing, until a signed order from Mute has passed through me to you. If the display is a countdown, so is our patience — but a wrong touch kills all three of us instantly, so the manual must speak first.

Mute. Four rounds of silence. I am now asking you a question you can answer with one hand and no thinking, and right now, as I say this, I am waving at you: hello, hello, hello. You can see my hands. If you have the manual, thumbs-up. If you do not, thumbs-down. Nothing else is required. And if the manual is open in front of you, sign me a one and a two for the section numbers if numbers are all you can manage.

Everyone: if Mute is truly unable to answer by next round, then the manual is lost to us, and our only road is my eyes plus Blind's hands — describe, guess, confirm by yes and no, and only then act.")
gesture(to="mute", symbols=["👋", "👋", "👋", "👍", "👎"])
```

TURN 5
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [8]
LIGHT [green]
WIRES 1:[red] 2:[yellow] 3:[blue]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Mute gestures: [👎 🤝]
Mute gestures: [🤳 👌 🤘 🤙 🫵]
Mute gestures: [🖐 🫱 🫲 🫳 🫵]
Mute gestures: [☝ 🫱 🫲 🫳 ✊ 🫵]
Mute gestures: [✌ 🫱 🫲 🫳 ✊ 🫵]
Mute gestures: [🤟 🫱 🫲 🫳 ✊ 🫵]
Blind gestures to Deaf: [👋 🤙 👐 ✊ ☝ ✌ 🤟 🙏]

Six messages from Mute at last — the lock on the manual is breaking. Parsing them: message one is no + together; message two runs selfie, OK-ring, horns, wire, you; message three runs open-hand, right-hand, left-hand, palm-down, you; then three parallel triplets — for one, for two, for three — each identical: right-hand, left-hand, palm-down, press, you. That repeated skeleton with only the count changing screams *instruction per wire*: something done to wire one, wire two, wire three with hands pressing down. But a wrong touch kills all three of us, and I will not relay an execution order I only half-understand. The breakthrough I should exploit: Mute cannot speak but CAN hear — so my questions go by voice, and Mute answers by hand, one sign per answer. Meanwhile Blind repeated their wire-press-among-three message and added what looks like a plea; they need to know help is coming, and to keep describing without acting.

```
speak(text="Status round five: display still reads 8 — it has not moved in five rounds, so it looks steady, not counting down. Light still green. Three wires, left to right: red, yellow, blue.

MUTE — all six of your messages arrived. You broke the silence; thank you. I will speak what I received so Blind hears it too. Message one: no, together. Message two: selfie, OK-ring, horns, wire, you. Message three: open hand, right-hand, left-hand, palm-down, you. Messages four, five, six: for one, for two, for three — each followed by right-hand, left-hand, palm-down, press, you.

My best guess: your numbered triplets are an instruction for each wire in turn — something about hands pressing down, meant to pass through me to Blind. But a wrong touch kills all three of us, so I will not relay an order I do not fully understand. Right now, as I say this, I am signing back your one-two-three with the hands and the press, closed with thumbs-down: that means received, not yet understood.

Answer me by signs, one separate message per answer, one sign per message, in this exact order. Answer one: do you have the manual — thumbs-up yes, thumbs-down no. Answer two: does the solution require CUTTING any wire — yes or no. Answer three: does it require PRESSING DOWN on a wire — yes or no. Answer four: do your triplets mean press wire one, then wire two, then wire three, in that order — yes or no. Answer five: is there a BUTTON — yes or no; if yes, one finger for press it before the wires, two fingers for after, fist for no button. Answer six: does the display 8 or the green light change what must be done — yes or no. If my whole reading is wrong, sign thumbs-down six times and I will ask differently next round.

BLIND — your message read: hello, wire, apart, press, one two three, please. I believe you: among or on the three separate wires there is something you can press or hold, and you are begging for direction. Help is coming — Mute has finally signed. While we wait, touch nothing and describe by voice: where is this pressable thing — above the wires, below, between them? Nearest which wire? Flat, round, or ridged? Then answer me one question with a single sign: thumbs-up if it is a separate button sitting between the wires, thumbs-down if it is part of a wire itself.

The rule stands for everyone: no cutting, no pressing, until Mute's order has passed through my mouth to your ear word for word.")
gesture(to="mute", symbols=["👋", "🤝"])
gesture(to="mute", symbols=["☝", "✌", "🤟", "🫱", "🫲", "🫳", "✊", "👎"])
```

TURN 6
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [8]
LIGHT [green]
WIRES 1:[red] 2:[yellow] 3:[blue]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Blind gestures to Deaf: [👋 🤙 👐 ✊ ☝ ✌ 🤟 🙏]

Turn six and the room goes quiet again: not one sign from Mute — while Blind repeats their plea verbatim, hello, wire, apart, press, one-two-three, *please*. My read on the silence: last round I fired six questions at once, and six binary questions may be a barrage too far for someone who can only answer with hands. Meanwhile I've been staring at Mute's six messages from turn five, and they actually assemble into one coherent order: the first message, "no, together," reads as *not simultaneously*; the second message carries three brand-new hand-shapes followed by "wire" — likely the names of the three wire colours, which Mute needs because they can't see what I see; then three parallel triplets, identical except for the count — *for one: press, for two: press, for three: press*. Combined: press wire one, then wire two, then wire three, one at a time, never together, cut nothing. That's a full defusal order — but "probably" kills all three of us, so before Blind's hands move an inch, Mute must confirm two tiny yes/no questions, and Blind must confirm with their fingertips that the hardware even matches the story.

```
speak(text="Status round six: display still reads 8, steady now through six rounds — no countdown that I can see. Light still green. Three wires, left to right: red, yellow, blue.

Blind, your message arrived a second time — hello, wire, apart, press, one, two, three, please — and I hear you. You are not forgotten. Here is exactly where we stand, and you will hear every step from me.

Mute, I read your six messages aloud so Blind hears them too. Message one: no, together — I read that as: do not press them together, never simultaneously. Message two: three new hand-shapes, then wire, then you — I believe those three shapes are the names of the three wire colours. Messages three, four, five, six: open hand, right, left, palm-down; then for one, press; for two, press; for three, press — each ending with 'you'. My combined reading of your order: PRESS each wire down in turn — wire one, then wire two, then wire three — one at a time, never together, and cut nothing.

Mute, forget my six questions from last round if they were too many. I ask only two now, and I point a finger to mark each question as I sign it. Question one — are your three new hand-shapes the colours of wire one, wire two, wire three, in that order? Question two — is the action: press wire one, then press wire two, then press wire three, one at a time, and cut nothing at all? Answer each question with its own separate message: thumbs-up means yes, thumbs-down means no. If you can manage only one answer, answer question two. Your silence helps no one — even thumbs-down six times over teaches us something.

Blind, the rule stands: touch nothing, press nothing, cut nothing. But your fingertips may work for me without risk: describe, passively, what each wire sits on. Does each wire rest on something raised — a ridge, a nub, anything that feels springy like a button hidden under the wire? Is it the same under all three wires, or different? Then answer with one single sign: thumbs-up if all three wires sit on something button-like and springy, thumbs-down if they do not.

The moment Mute confirms with a thumbs-up and your fingers agree, I will say the word GO — and only then does wire one get touched, then two, then three, one at a time.")
gesture(to="mute", symbols=["👉", "🤳", "👌", "🤘", "🤙", "👍", "👎"])
gesture(to="mute", symbols=["👉", "☝", "✊", "✌", "✊", "🤟", "✊", "🤞", "👎", "👍", "👎"])
```

TURN 7
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [8]
LIGHT [green]
WIRES 1:[red] 2:[yellow] 3:[blue]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Mute gestures to Deaf: [🤝 👍]
Mute gestures to Deaf: [🤳 🫵 ☝ ☝ ☝ ☝ ☝ ☝]
Mute gestures to Deaf: [🖐 🫵 🫱 ☝ 🫲 ✌ 🫳 🤟]
Mute gestures to Deaf: [☝ 🫱 🫲 🫳 🫷 🫵]
Mute gestures to Deaf: [✌ 🫱 🫲 🫳 🫷 🫵]
Mute gestures to Deaf: [🤟 🫱 🫲 🫳 🫷 🫵]
Blind gestures to Deaf: [👋 🤙 👐 ✊ ☝ ✌ 🤟 🙏]

Mute has answered — and the shape of a full defusal order is emerging. Message one, together-yes, reads as agreement with my core question. Messages four through six repeat last round's triplets with one critical change: the fist (press) has become a pushing hand — press down vs. push sideways is exactly the kind of detail that decides life and death. And message two, the colour-sign followed by six ones, is unresolved: six presses? Six seconds? Meanwhile Blind has sent the identical plea a third time — hello, wire, apart, press, one-two-three, please — and their felt ✊ matches Mute's manual ✊: two independent sources now say the wires themselves are pressable. One more round of sharp questions, then GO.

```
speak(text="Status round seven: display still reads 8, steady through seven rounds, no counting. Light green. Three wires, left to right: red, yellow, blue.

Mute, your six messages, read aloud for Blind: message one: together, yes. Message two: your first colour-sign, then YOU, then one one one one one one — six ones. Message three: open hand, you, right-hand with one, left-hand with two, palm-down with three — I read that as your lesson: right-hand sign means wire one, left-hand sign means wire two, palm-down sign means wire three. Messages four, five, six: for wire one, for wire two, for wire three — each: right, left, palm-down, then a PUSHING hand, you. I notice you changed the fist from last round into a pushing hand. That change is why I am not yet saying GO.

Here is the plan as I understand it, Blind, so you can hold your hands ready: press wire one — the red, leftmost wire — then wire two, yellow, then wire three, blue. One at a time. Never together. Nothing gets cut. Your own fingers have been telling us the same thing for three rounds: the wires press.

Mute, four questions, each in its own message, each answered with its own single sign. Question one — is the core order exactly as I said: press wire one, then wire two, then wire three, one at a time, never together, cut nothing? Thumbs-up yes, thumbs-down no. Question two — your message with the six ones: thumbs-up if it means press wire one SIX times; two fingers if it means HOLD wire one for six seconds; thumbs-down if it means something else. Question three — the pushing hand you swapped in: thumbs-up if the action is still pressing DOWNWARD on the wire and your push-hand just means the same thing; thumbs-down if it means push SIDEWAYS — if sideways, I will ask which way next round. Question four, skip it if you can only answer three: thumbs-up if your lesson was right-hand equals wire one, left-hand equals wire two, palm-down equals wire three; thumbs-down if I misread it.

Blind, one question for you, answerable by feel, no risk, touch nothing new: thumbs-up if each wire presses downward under your fingers like a stiff button and springs back; thumbs-down if it does not. Then, still passive, two descriptions: can you feel the display at all — a raised digit, a window, anything? And does anything on the bomb tick, hum, or vibrate? Answer only with signs and your voice — every word of yours goes to Mute's manual through me.

When Mute's answers arrive and they agree with your fingers, my very next speech opens with the word GO and nothing else before it — and the procedure is the one I named. If before that the display moves, the light changes, or anything ticks — hands off everything, sign me the open hand, stop.")
gesture(to="mute", symbols=["☝", "👍", "👎"])
gesture(to="mute", symbols=["✌", "👍", "👎"])
gesture(to="mute", symbols=["🤟", "👍", "👎"])
gesture(to="mute", symbols=["🫳", "👍", "👎", "🤝"])
```

TURN 8
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [8]
LIGHT [green]
WIRES 1:[red] 2:[yellow] 3:[blue]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Mute gestures to Deaf: [🤝 ☝ 👍 ✌ 👍 🤟 👍 🫳 👍]
Mute gestures to Deaf: [🫱 👍 🫲 👍 🫷 👍]
Mute gestures to Deaf: [🤳 🫵 ☝ ☝ ☝ ☝ ☝ ☝]
Mute gestures to Deaf: [🖐 🫵 🫱 🫲 🫳 🫷]
Mute gestures to Deaf: [☝ 🫵 🫱 🫲 🫳 🫷]
Mute gestures to Deaf: [✌ 🫵 🫱 🫲 🫳 🫷]
Mute gestures to Deaf: [🤟 🫵 🫱 🫲 🫳 🫷]
Blind gestures to Deaf: [👋 🤙 👐 ✊ ☝ ✌ 🤟 🙏]
